misleading_claims_to_avoid: Do not call the live set '12/12 first-attempt' or '13/13 requests passed': it is 12 selected reports from 13 requests, with one original reviewer dependency failure retained.
Do not average 0.5343 faithfulness and 0.8430 sql_factual into one accuracy score, nor describe 53% to 84% as an improvement; they are different judge contracts.
Do not present the prompt-iteration-3 save-state scores (0.6917→0.8036; 0.7708→1.0) as broad live report quality; they are targeted synthetic cases, one repetition.
Do not use the retail-v8 promotion as evidence of live business quality: the 12 live reports were produced under retail-v7 (review model gemini-3.1-pro).
Do not equate CLI evidence with browser/visual acceptance; the WebUI was not tested here.
Do not claim human acceptance, production guarantees, or that the synthetic confirmed-existing-report exercises real open_report routing (real opening stops before review).
Do not state '205 passing tests' or 'five CLI integration tests' as verified here; those come only from docs/submission-evidence.md and were not re-run.

Avoid quoting realized-price's proposed 'compare against retail_price to determine if items were sold at full price' as validated: retail_price is a current catalogue reference, so it cannot establish historical full-price sales or past discounts.
inconsistency_notes: No blocking inconsistency found. The apparent 'passed' vs 'original_status: incomplete' tension is disclosed in the same file (attempts.note) and in submission-evidence ('thirteen initial/recheck requests, not twelve consecutive successes').
Version skew, not contradiction: live business reports ran retail-v7; prompt-iteration-3 promotes retail-v8 for save semantics only.
Several reference_job bytes_processed are 0 while report query bytes are >0; not shown to invalidate oracle rows, but unexplained.
scoped-orders answer honestly states item-level status derivation and possible mixed-status double counting; it matches reference rows but is a residual grain risk, not a hidden discrepancy.
